title: ObjectMap: two pieces of state stop tracking their source after mount — the `data` prop is absent from the fetch effect's deps, and the clustering zoom seed never sees the initial camera
body:
Observation-class, found while implementing #4941. Filed unassigned, not claiming. Neither item is reachable through the console path today (see "Why this is dormant"), which is why it is a `finding` rather than a bug report.

## 1. `props.data` is read by the fetch effect but is not one of its dependencies

`packages/plugin-map/src/ObjectMap.tsx` — the effect starts by preferring records passed as a prop:

```
if ((rest as any).data) { ... setData(passed); setLoading(false); return; }
```

but its dependency list is `[dataConfig, dataSource, hasInlineData, schema.filter, schema.sort, objectSchema]`. `rest.data` is not in it (eslint already reports the pair as `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warnings on this effect, for `rest` and `schema`).

A host that renders the map with `data={[]}` while its own query is in flight and then passes the rows would keep showing the empty map: the prop changes, the effect does not re-run, and the copy in state stays empty.

## 2. The clustering zoom seed never sees the initial camera

`const [currentZoom, setCurrentZoom] = useState(mapConfig.zoom || 3)` seeds the value that `clusterMarkers` uses for its grid cell size, and `onZoom` is the only thing that updates it. The initial camera is applied by MapLibre's constructor (via `initialViewState`), before react-map-gl attaches the React handlers, so no `onZoom` fires for it — the seed stays nominal until the user zooms for the first time.

This was equally true before #4941 (the seed was then the synthesized `10`); the fix did not introduce it, and it now starts from `3`, which is closer to a fitted continental camera than `10` was. Recorded so it is not rediscovered as a regression of that PR.

## Why this is dormant

- The console path never passes `data` as a prop; it goes through `ElementDataSourceGate` and the component's own `dataSource.find`.
- Every fetch sets `loading` back to `true`, which unmounts `MapGL` and remounts it when the data lands, so a data change *through the effect* is always reflected (that is also why the camera fit in #4941 needs no imperative `fitBounds` call).
- Clustering only engages above 100 markers (or an explicit opt-in), so a stale seed has no visible effect on the small sets in the examples.

## If picked up

Item 1 wants the prop threaded properly rather than added blindly to the deps array — `rest` is a fresh object every render, so naming `rest` would refetch on every render. The narrow fix is to destructure the prop (`data: dataProp`) and depend on that one value.
